November 25, 2026 © Adobe Stock/Halina A record 2,100-plus migrants arrived in Spain's Canary Islands over 24 hours in overcrowded boats, maritime rescue service data showed on Wednesday, prompting regional leader Fernando Clavijo to call for a European-level response to the crisis. "The Canaries can't take it anymore. We're experiencing an unprecedented migration pressure," Clavijo wrote on X, adding that he had requested an urgent meeting with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. "These people come to Europe and it's not fair that we alone respond to a drama of this magnitude," he said. One migrant was found dead in a boat and another gave birth during the perilous crossing from West Africa, the rescue service said. The daily arrivals surpassed the previous record of about 1,500 set two weeks ago. Most of the boats arrived at El Hierro, an island of some 11,400 residents that has become one of Europe's key entry points for migrants from West Africa. Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, who has faced tough criticism of his open stance on migration during the campaign ahead of Sunday's parliamentary election, said on Wednesday Europe needed a comprehensive approach to migration, including stronger border controls in cooperation with Senegalese and Gambian authorities. Still, he said Spain needed "to open legal migration pathways" for workers in sectors such as housing that are short of qualified labour. The Atlantic route from West Africa to the Canary Islands is one of the world's deadliest migration crossings as migrants seek to reach Spanish territory despite rough seas, strong currents and long distances. Arrivals tend to pick up in the autumn months, when sea conditions along the route are generally calmer and more favourable for crossings. Arrivals so far this year had climbed to 28,103 as of late November, more than last year's total but still well below an all-time high of 46,843 recorded in 2024, when most crossings occurred during the first nine months of the year. Nearly 21,000 people have reached the archipelago in the last two months. (Reuters)

articles.title: NYK Line, Partners to Advance Remote Ship Emissions Monitoring
articles.summary: Shipping company NYK Line and seven other organizations have signed an agreement to develop remote sensing technology capable of measuring greenhouse gas emissions from vessels without physical contact, with trials focused on Yokohama Port in Japan.The agreement…
articles.body: NYK Line, Partners to Advance Remote Ship Emissions Monitoring Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 25, 2026 Conceptual image of the system (Credit: NYK Line) Shipping company NYK Line and seven other organizations have signed an agreement to develop remote sensing technology capable of measuring greenhouse gas emissions from vessels without physical contact, with trials focused on Yokohama Port in Japan. The agreement, signed on November 25, brings together NYK Line, MUFG Bank, Nagoya Electric Works, ArkEdge Space, Shimizu Corporation, the City of Yokohama, Yokohama-Kawasaki International Port Corporation and Yokohama Port Corporation. The collaboration will advance the True Emission Eye - Maritime project, which aims to develop technology for measuring, visualizing and quantifying greenhouse gas emissions from ships at a distance. The project will conduct measurements on actual vessels at Yokohama Port to assess the technology's accuracy, while examining system specifications, potential applications and opportunities for future commercial deployment. The technology is being developed to complement existing methods of estimating vessel emissions based on fuel type and consumption, providing a means of directly measuring emissions from outside ships. The system uses optical observation technology that exploits the ability of gases, including carbon dioxide, to absorb and emit light at specific wavelengths. Data obtained from vessel exhaust observations is combined with physical parameters, including distance to the ship and weather conditions, to calculate emissions. Testing has already been conducted at experimental facilities and on NYK Group vessels, both at berth and underway. At Yokohama Port, the project has captured infrared images of ship exhaust from observation points including Osanbashi Pier and the Yokohama Bay Bridge Skywalk. The images are being compared and analyzed against vessel data to evaluate the technology. The partners will continue conducting measurements under different conditions to improve the accuracy of the system, while also examining fixed-point monitoring at ports. The project will also assess the technical requirements for satellite-based observations of ship emissions and explore the potential integration of satellite measurements with ground-based data. The eight organizations aim to bring the technology into practical use to improve transparency in vessel emissions reporting and support decarbonization across the shipping and port sectors.

articles.summary: A record three-quarters of the global fleet of large tankers designed to transport oil products are tapping higher earnings to ship crude, keeping the cost to move fuels elevated.

Join the leading maritime news network Photo: Avigator Thailand/Shutterstock By Weilun Soon Nov 25, 2026 (Bloomberg) –A record three-quarters of the global fleet of large tankers designed to transport oil products are tapping higher earnings to ship crude, keeping the cost to move fuels elevated. Less than a quarter of the world’s 542 long-range 2, or LR2, tankers are currently transporting “clean” cargoes such as jet fuel, naphtha and diesel as of this week, according to Signal Ocean data. The vessels have cargo holds that are coated to transport refined fuels, and have to undergo an expensive cleaning process to return to the trade once they ship “dirty” crude oil. The shift in use of the LR2 fleet comes as crude flows recover through the Strait of Hormuz. A system of shuttling tankers and ship-to-ship transfers has helped exports from the Persian Gulf recover to pre-war levels, boosting freight rates and prompting charterers to tap smaller vessels to meet demand. Benchmark earnings for very-large crude carriers have soared, in turn enabling smaller-sized tankers — including Aframaxes, which are the crude-focused equivalent of LR2s, able to hold about 750,000 barrels — to command far higher fees. And an LR2 that dirties up can charge Aframax earnings. Shipping executives often look at how many LR2s are switching to plan on how much they can charge, and how they should deploy their tankers around the world. Even though the LR2 fleet has grown 12% since January last year and clean-fuel shipments have fallen due to the US-Iran war, the increased switching to crude has helped put a floor underneath the fees they can command to carry oil products. “Tracking LR2 employment between clean and dirty trades is becoming as important as monitoring the size of the fleet itself,” Signal analysts Maria Bertzeletou and Georgios Sakellariou said. The switching of LR2s started last year as traders sought to store more crude on vessels at sea, but accelerated in the initial phase of the Iran War from the end of February, when refineries in the Middle East were attacked by the Islamic Republic — reducing the need for clean tankers, Sakellariou said. About 1.7 million out of the more than 9 million barrels a day of refining capacity is currently offline in the Middle East, RBC Capital Markets analysts including Christopher Louney and Helima Croft wrote in a note this week. Around 1 million barrels a day of that potentially needs months to repair, they said. Charterers are turning to smaller product tankers, with the share of LR2s in transporting fuels falling to just 12% between July and September, from almost 18% a year earlier, Signal data show. Join the leading maritime news network On 24 November 2026, Windcat signed a contract with Damen Shipyards Group for the second Multi-Purpose Accommodation Support Vessel (MP-ASV) in the Innovation Series. The contract follows the order for the first vessel , with an option for five more, signed in November last year. Sound basis The MP-ASV is an entirely new type of vessel designed to support operations in the offshore energy industry . Its design draws heavily on Damen’s experience in the design and construction of Commissioning Services Operations Vessels (CSOVs). This includes the Elevation Series CSOVs, developed together by Damen and Windcat. The first vessel in the Elevation Series, Windcat Rotterdam , was presented with the KNVTS Ship of the Year Award at this year’s Maritime Awards Gala. The MP-ASV takes the proven capabilities of the Elevation Series CSOVs and builds on them further. Extended capabilities The MP-ASVs build on these capabilities in a number of ways, including with their 102 x 20 metre hull and its 750m 2 deck space. The MP-ASV is able to assist and operate in all offshore energy markets, including cable repair, flotel functions, offshore wind and ROV assistance. Additionally, the vessel is fitted with 111 cabins, allowing up to 190 persons on board. The vessel features an offshore crane which can be used as a 150-tonne subsea crane, or as a 15-tonne 3D motion-compensated crane. The vessel can also be fitted with remotely operated vehicles (ROVs). The vessels are being equipped with a DP2+ system holding DNV CBS and CBT class notations, which cover a wider scope of redundant closed bus-ties system arrangements, for enhanced fault tolerance. The DP system features additional tunnel thrusters fore and aft to provide increased redundancy for safe operations in remote offshore locations. Access is via a 3D motion-compensated gangway with two exchangeable tips, one for short connections used in the wind industry and one capable of long continuous connections. Prepared for efficiency The MP-ASVs will be outfitted with a battery system to enable peak shaving, spinning reserve and electrical sailing. This will enable highly efficient operations, for example when in DP mode. Like the Windcat CSOVs, a key feature of the Innovation Series vessels is the integration of low-carbon fuels . Hence a dual fuel hydrogen auxiliary genset is installed, and the three main generator sets are of the next generation Evolve generator sets from ABC, which allow for a range of low-emission possibilities. These engines can operate on liquid fuels such as biodiesel and HVO, on dual fuel with pilot injection of liquid fuel, or on 100% gas using spark ignition. High offshore comfort level The design of the vessel is also highly focused on comfort for the up to 190 personnel onboard. Measures include well-thought-out routing, use of high-quality materials and aesthetically appealing accommodation. The aim is to make crew and personnel feel at home during extended periods of up to 150 days offshore, due to her extended fuel capacity. Strength-to-strength Damen Sales Director Joost van der Weiden says, “We are delighted to receive this second MP-ASV order from Windcat. The cooperation that began with our development of the Elevation Series continues to grow in strength. With the Innovation Series we mutually have developed a vessel that will further enhance Windcat’s capabilities to support its clients in the offshore energy industry in the years ahead.” Windcat Managing Director Willem van der Wel says: “The decision to order a second MP-ASV reflects our confidence in this new vessel concept and our ambition to further strengthen our position in the offshore energy market. By combining the capabilities of a multi-purpose support vessel with high-quality offshore accommodation, we are creating a versatile solution that responds to the evolving needs of our customers. articles.title: Petronas Names ‘World's First’ Nearshore FLNG Facility
articles.summary: Petronas has officially named its third floating liquefied natural gas (FLNG) facility, PFLNG TIGA, at Samsung Heavy Industries' shipyard in South Korea, ahead of its planned deployment to Malaysia and start-up in the third quarter of 2027.Described…
articles.body: Petronas Names ‘World's First’ Nearshore FLNG Facility Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 25, 2026 (Credit: Petronas) Petronas has officially named its third floating liquefied natural gas (FLNG) facility, PFLNG TIGA, at Samsung Heavy Industries' shipyard in South Korea, ahead of its planned deployment to Malaysia and start-up in the third quarter of 2027. Described by Petronas as the world's first nearshore FLNG facility, PFLNG TIGA is currently under construction at the shipyard on Geoje Island and will be deployed to Sipitang, Sabah, Malaysia. The facility is designed to produce 2 million tonnes of LNG annually and measures 281 metres in length, 64 metres in width and 32 metres in depth. PFLNG TIGA will become the third floating LNG facility developed by Petronas , expanding its portfolio of facilities designed for shallow-water, deepwater and nearshore environments. The new facility is intended to support the development and commercialisation of gas resources while strengthening Malaysia's LNG supply capabilities. Petronas said the addition would provide greater flexibility in bringing gas resources to market and meeting regional and international demand. The company has been active in the LNG industry for more than four decades, with PFLNG TIGA representing another addition to its integrated LNG portfolio.

November 25, 2026 © Miha Creative / Adobe Stock Crude oil prices fell on Wednesday as the prospect of a market surplus offset concerns about disruptions to oil exports in the Middle East. Brent crude futures LCOc1 declined 44 cents, or 0.5%, to $90.96 a barrel at 1035 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate crude futures CLc1 slipped 62 cents, or 0.8%, to $81.43 a barrel. Both benchmarks gained more than 2% on Tuesday. "Investors are preoccupied with the thought of supply exceeding demand," said Tamas Varga, an oil analyst at PVM, a brokerage. On Wednesday, Yemen's Houthis said they had attacked Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil refinery ‌and Riyadh's financial district. Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia's largest refinery, is part of a complex on the kingdom's Gulf coast ‌that ⁠also serves as a major export terminal for Saudi crude. A build-up in crude inventories is also contributing to the softer oil prices, Varga said. US crude stocks rose by 126,000 barrels in the week ended November 20, market sources said on Tuesday, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute. API/S Eight analysts polled by Reuters estimated that crude inventories rose by about 1.5 million barrels on average. "Uncertainty about OPEC's 2027 policies in the upcoming November 29 meeting, especially with the UAE no longer restricted by OPEC+ policies and Iraq seeking higher oil output capacity, as well as broader market risk-off are some reasons," said Zhenqiang Seto, a senior research specialist for oil at LSEG. OPEC+ ministers will hold a series of meetings on November 29 to decide on their 2027 output policy. "Since the release of an IEA report this month, perceptions of a global supply glut have kept prices in check," said Tsuyoshi Ueno, senior economist at NLI Research Institute. Attention is also focused on how next year's production quotas will be determined at the OPEC+ meeting, Ueno said. Iraq is pressing OPEC+ to lift its estimate of the country's crude oil production capacity, four people familiar with the matter said, heightening tensions over a review that will help determine how much members can pump next year. Libya's Sharara oil pipeline has also reopened after an "unlawful group" closed a valve on the pipeline, with oil beginning to flow into storage tanks at the Akakus facility in Zawiya. "However, attacks on ships near the Strait of Hormuz and exchanges of attacks between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis have raised uncertainty over the sustainability of this trend," Ueno said. A container ship was targeted and came to a stop on Tuesday while sailing an "unauthorised" route near the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said, according to state media. On Monday, three vessels were struck by unidentified projectiles as they sailed east through the strait, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said on Tuesday. articles.body: Windcat Expands Offshore Fleet with Second Damen Multi-Purpose Vessel Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 25, 2026 (Credit: Windcat) Windcat has signed a contract with Damen Shipyards Group for a second Multi-Purpose Accommodation Support Vessel (MP-ASV) under its Innovation Series, expanding its planned fleet of vessels designed for offshore energy operations. The agreement, signed on November 24, follows Windcat's initial order in November 2025 for the first vessel in the series, which included an option for five additional units. The new MP-ASV design builds on the companies' earlier collaboration on the Elevation Series commissioning service operations vessels (CSOVs), incorporating additional capabilities for offshore wind, subsea cable repair, offshore accommodation and remotely operated vehicle (ROV) support. The vessels will measure 102 meters in length and 20 meters in width, with approximately 750 square meters of deck space and 111 cabins accommodating up to 190 personnel. Each MP-ASV will feature an offshore crane capable of operating as a 150-tonne subsea crane or a 15-tonne three-dimensional motion-compensated crane, alongside provisions for ROV installation. Personnel transfers will be supported by a 3D motion-compensated gangway with interchangeable tips designed for short connections in offshore wind operations and longer continuous connections. The vessels will also feature a DP2+ dynamic positioning system with DNV CBS and CBT class notations, incorporating additional bow and stern tunnel thrusters to improve redundancy during offshore operations. The propulsion and power arrangement will include a battery system for peak shaving, spinning reserve and electrical sailing, together with a dual-fuel hydrogen auxiliary generator. Three main generator sets supplied by ABC will feature its Evolve technology, designed to accommodate different fuel options, including biodiesel, hydrotreated vegetable oil (HVO), dual-fuel operation and gas. The MP-ASVs are designed for extended offshore deployments of up to 150 days, supported by increased fuel capacity and accommodation facilities intended for prolonged stays at sea. The Innovation Series builds on Damen and Windcat's Elevation Series partnership, which includes the Windcat Rotterdam, named KNVTS Ship of the Year at the 2026 Maritime Awards Gala.

articles.title: NextGeo Gets $12.7M Offshore Survey Job for Spain-France Hydrogen Link
articles.summary: Italian offshore services provider Next Geosolutions (NextGeo) has secured a contract worth approximately $12.7 million (€11.6 million) from BarMar for offshore survey work supporting the development of a planned hydrogen pipeline connecting…
articles.body: NextGeo Gets $12.7M Offshore Survey Job for Spain-France Hydrogen Link Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 25, 2026 Italian offshore services provider Next Geosolutions (NextGeo) has secured a contract worth approximately $12.7 million (€11.6 million) from BarMar for offshore survey work supporting the development of a planned hydrogen pipeline connecting Spain and France. The contract covers an integrated survey campaign along an approximately 366-kilometre offshore corridor between Barcelona, Spain, and Fos-sur-Mer, France. The scope includes geophysical, geotechnical and UXO surveys, grab sampling, remotely operated vehicle (ROV) inspections and surveys of crossings with existing subsea infrastructure. The data collected will be used to characterise seabed and sub-seabed conditions to support the planning and design of the future pipeline. NextGeo will deploy two dedicated vessels for the offshore operations, which are expected to begin by the end of 2026. The campaign is currently scheduled for completion between the end of the second quarter and the beginning of the third quarter of 2027, depending on any additional work requested during execution. The BarMar pipeline forms part of H2med, a cross-border initiative designed to connect hydrogen networks in the Iberian Peninsula with northwestern Europe. The project is being developed by BarMar S.A.S., whose shareholders are NaTran, Enagás and Teréga. H2med is included on the European Union's list of Projects of Common Interest, with BarMar providing the planned maritime hydrogen transport connection between Spain and France. The award marks NextGeo's first contract with BarMar, expanding its offshore survey activities into hydrogen infrastructure development.
